title.zh: 卷371 列傳一百五十八 颜伯焘 怡良 祁宇 黄恩彤 刘韵珂 牛鑑
title.en: Volume 371 Biographies 158: Yan Bodao, Yi Liang, Qi Yu, Huang Entong, Liu Yunke, Niu Jian
title.raw: 卷371 列傳一百五十八 颜伯焘 怡良 祁宇 黄恩彤 刘韵珂 牛鑑

sentences.zh: =顏伯燾=顏伯燾，字魯輿，廣東連平人，巡撫希深孫，總督檢子。

translations.literal: Yan Bozao, style name Luyu, was a native of Lianping in Guangdong, grandson of the provincial governor Xishen and son of the governor-general Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bozao, whose style was Luyu, came from Lianping in Guangdong. He was the grandson of Governor Xishen and the son of Governor-General Yan Jian.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the nineteenth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received appointment as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，出為陝西延榆綏道、督糧道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he went out as intendant of the Yan-Yu-Sui Circuit in Shaanxi and grain transport intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 he was posted as intendant of Shaanxi's Yan-Yu-Sui Circuit and as grain transport intendant.

sentences.zh: 歷陝西按察使，甘肅、直隸布政使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Shaanxi provincial judicial commissioner and as provincial treasurer of Gansu and Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Shaanxi judicial commissioner and provincial treasurer in Gansu and Zhili.

sentences.zh: 大軍徵回疆，以轉運勞，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned in the Western Regions, he was rewarded with a peacock feather for his transport labors.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign in the Western Regions he earned a peacock feather for his work on supply transport.

sentences.zh: 署陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: He acted as Shaanxi provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授雲南巡撫，改建滇池石徬，農田賴之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Yunnan provincial governor; he rebuilt the stone embankment at Dianchi Lake, on which farmland relied.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he became governor of Yunnan and rebuilt the stone dike at Dianchi Lake, which the surrounding fields depended on.

sentences.zh: 兼署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: He also acted as governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as acting governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 伯燾累世膺疆寄，嫺習吏治，所至有聲。

translations.literal: Bozao's family for generations had held frontier commissions; he was skilled in administration, and wherever he went he gained a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His family had held frontier posts for generations, and he was adept at governance; wherever he served he won renown.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時定海已陷，伯燾至，劾水師提督陳階平於英兵前次攻廈門告病規避，又論琦善主款僨事，及林則徐守粵功罪。

translations.literal: At that time Dinghai had already fallen; when Bozao arrived he impeached the naval commander Chen Jieping for reporting illness to evade duty when the English troops had earlier attacked Xiamen, and also discussed Qishan's leading the peace negotiations and borrowing, and the merits and faults of Lin Zexu's defense of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai had already fallen by then. On reaching his post Bozao impeached Naval Commander Chen Jieping for feigning illness to avoid fighting when the British had earlier attacked Xiamen, and he also weighed Qishan's leadership of peace talks and borrowing against Lin Zexu's record in defending Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，奏請餉銀二百萬，造船募新兵及水勇八千，以備出洋禦敵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he memorialized requesting two million taels of pay silver, building ships, recruiting new troops and eight thousand naval braves, to prepare for going to sea to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he asked for two million taels of pay, new warships, recruits, and eight thousand naval militia so the fleet could go out to meet the enemy at sea.

sentences.zh: 复疏陳廣東兵事​​，略曰：「閩、粵互為脣齒，呼吸相通。

translations.literal: He again memorialized on Guangdong military affairs, saying in summary: "Fujian and Guangdong are lip and teeth to each other, breathing in common.
translations.idiomatic: He sent another memorial on the fighting in Guangdong, writing in part: "Fujian and Guangdong are as lip to teeth; what touches one is felt at once in the other.

sentences.zh: 自正月虎門不守，粵事幾不可問。

translations.literal: Since the first month, when Humen could not be held, Guangdong affairs were nearly beyond inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Since Humen fell in the first month, affairs in Guangdong have been all but hopeless.

sentences.zh: 四月內夷船駛泊省西泥城，防勇望風潰遁，兵船被焚，砲台棄去。

translations.literal: Within the fourth month foreign ships anchored west of the provincial capital at Nicheng; defending braves fled at sight of the wind, war junks were burned, and batteries were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month foreign vessels anchored at Nicheng west of the provincial capital. The defenders broke and ran, warships were burned, and the batteries were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 當事者以洋銀六百萬元令知府餘保純重啗敵人，始允罷戰，猶報勝仗，指為就撫，以欺朝廷。

translations.literal: Those in charge used six million dollars in foreign silver and had Prefect Yu Baochun heavily bribe the enemy before they would agree to cease fighting; they still reported victories, calling it submission secured, to deceive the court.
translations.idiomatic: The officials in charge paid six million dollars in foreign silver and sent Prefect Yu Baochun to bribe the enemy heavily before fighting stopped. They still reported victories and called it a successful pacification, deceiving the court.

sentences.zh: 夫撫非不可，然必痛剿之後，始能帖伏。

translations.literal: Pacification is not impossible, yet only after severe punitive campaigns can they be made to submit peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification is not impossible, but the enemy will submit only after they have been struck hard.

sentences.zh: 今逆勢方張，資之庫藏，何不以養士卒？

translations.literal: Now the rebels' momentum is just rising—why supply their treasury? Why not use it to support the troops?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's power is still rising. Why fill their coffers when the same treasure could feed our soldiers?

sentences.zh: 如謂曲徇商民所請，何不於誓師之始，申效死之義，與之同守？

translations.literal: If one says this bent to the requests of merchants and people, why at the beginning of the army's oath-taking did one not proclaim the duty to die in service and defend together with them?
translations.idiomatic: If the plea was that merchants and townspeople had to be indulged, why at the oath-taking before battle did the commanders not call on everyone to die in defense and stand with them?

sentences.zh: 粵民非不可用，前有蕭關、三元里等鄉數千人圍困義律，乃餘保純出城彈壓，始漸散去。

translations.literal: Guangdong people are not unusable; earlier several thousand men from villages such as Xiaoguan and Sanyuanli besieged Elliot, but then Yu Baochun went out of the city to suppress them, and only then did they gradually disperse.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong are not useless. Thousands from Xiaoguan, Sanyuanli, and other villages had once surrounded Elliot, but Yu Baochun went out of the city to suppress them, and only then did the crowd slowly disperse.

sentences.zh: 保純以議撫之後，不應妄生枝節，是謂六百萬之資可以求安也。

translations.literal: Baochun, because peace talks had been agreed, said one should not rashly create complications—meaning that six million in funds could buy security.
translations.idiomatic: Baochun argued that once peace talks had begun there must be no fresh trouble—that six million dollars could simply buy safety.

sentences.zh: 奕山、隆文已遠避數十里，楊芳，齊慎亦退入城。

translations.literal: Yishan and Longwen had already fled far off for several tens of li; Yang Fang and Qi Shen also withdrew into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan and Longwen had already withdrawn dozens of li away, and Yang Fang and Qi Shen had retreated into the city as well.

sentences.zh: 奕山、隆文等閱歷未深，楊芳年老耳聾，皆不足當重任。

translations.literal: Yishan, Longwen, and the like had shallow experience; Yang Fang was old and deaf—all were insufficient to bear heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan and Longwen lacked experience, and Yang Fang was old and hard of hearing; none of them was fit for so grave a charge.

sentences.zh: 斯時惟有特簡親信重臣，督造船砲，用本省之人，作本省之兵，懸以重賞，未有不堪一用者。

translations.literal: At this time only by specially selecting a trusted senior minister to supervise building ships and cannon, using men of the province as the province's troops, and hanging out heavy rewards would there be none who could not be put to use.
translations.idiomatic: At such a moment the court should appoint a trusted senior minister to oversee ships and guns, raise troops from the province itself, and offer rich rewards—then there would be no force that could not be made useful.

sentences.zh: 臣移駐廈門，督修戰具，但使船砲稍備，即當奮力攻擊，不敢老師糜餉，以取咎戾。」

translations.literal: Your servant will move his headquarters to Xiamen and supervise repair of war equipment; once ships and cannon are somewhat ready, he will at once strive to attack, not daring to keep the army idle and waste pay to incur blame."
translations.idiomatic: I shall move my headquarters to Xiamen and oversee the repair of weapons. As soon as ships and guns are even partly ready I shall strike with all my strength and will not keep the army idle wasting pay to invite reproach."

sentences.zh: 又薦裕謙、林則徐可任粵事。

translations.literal: He also recommended Yijing and Lin Zexu as able to take charge of Guangdong affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Yijing and Lin Zexu as men fit to handle Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 伯燾主戰甚力，欲一當敵。

translations.literal: Bozao advocated war with great force and wished to meet the enemy once for all.
translations.idiomatic: Bozao pressed hard for war and was eager to give the enemy a decisive fight.

sentences.zh: 七月，英兵三十餘艘犯廈門，投書索為外埠，即駛入攻擊，接戰，毀敵輪船一、兵艇五，敵遂聚攻砲台，總兵江繼芸、游擊凌志、都司張然、守備王世俊皆死之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month more than thirty English ships attacked Xiamen, sent a letter demanding it as an outer port, then sailed in to attack; in battle they destroyed one enemy steamship and five gunboats; the enemy then massed to attack the batteries, and Regional Commander Jiang Jiyun, Mobile Corps Commander Ling Zhi, Brigade Commander Zhang Ran, and Garrison Commander Wang Shijun all died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month more than thirty British vessels attacked Xiamen, demanded in writing that it be opened as an outer port, and at once sailed in to fight. In the engagement one enemy steamer and five gunboats were destroyed. The British then concentrated on the batteries. Regional Commander Jiang Jiyun, Mobile Corps Commander Ling Zhi, Brigade Commander Zhang Ran, and Garrison Commander Wang Shijun were all killed.

sentences.zh: 伯燾所募水勇，以節餉議遣，未有安置。

translations.literal: The naval braves Bozao had recruited, because of economizing pay, were discussed for dismissal and had not yet been placed.
translations.idiomatic: The naval militia Bozao had raised were under discussion for dismissal to save pay and had not yet been settled anywhere.

sentences.zh: 當戰時，呼噪應敵，英兵登岸，以台砲回擊，廈門官署街市並毀，伯燾退保同安。

translations.literal: During the fighting they shouted and answered the enemy; English troops landed and were struck back with battery cannon; Xiamen's government offices and markets were together destroyed, and Bozao withdrew to hold Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting they shouted and rushed to meet the enemy. When British troops landed, battery guns were turned on them, but Xiamen's offices and markets were wrecked together, and Bozao fell back to Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 英人得廈門不之守，越數日，移船赴浙洋，惟留數艘泊鼓浪嶼。

translations.literal: The English having taken Xiamen did not hold it; after several days they moved their ships to Zhejiang waters, leaving only several vessels anchored at Gulangyu.
translations.idiomatic: The British took Xiamen but did not garrison it. A few days later they shifted their fleet toward Zhejiang, leaving only a few ships at Gulangyu.

sentences.zh: 詔斥不能豫防，倉猝失事，以廈門收復，免其治罪，議革職，從寬降三品頂戴留任。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him for inability to take precautions and for losing affairs in haste; because Xiamen was recovered he was exempted from punishment by law; dismissal from office was discussed, but leniently he was reduced to third-rank cap button and retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked him for failing to prepare and for the sudden disaster, but because Xiamen was recovered he was spared criminal punishment. Dismissal was considered, yet he was leniently reduced to third-rank insignia and kept in office.

sentences.zh: 尋命侍郎端華至閩察勘，坐未能進剿罷職，時論仍右之。

translations.literal: Soon Vice Minister Duanhua was ordered to Fujian to inspect; Bozao was dismissed from office on the charge of failing to advance and attack, yet public opinion still favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Vice Minister Duanhua was sent to Fujian to investigate. Bozao was dismissed for failing to press the attack, but opinion still favored him.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，召來京，將起用，道梗不得至，尋病卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was summoned to the capital and was about to be reemployed, but the roads were blocked and he could not arrive; soon he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 he was called to the capital for reappointment, but the roads were blocked and he could not reach Beijing. He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子鍾驥，宣統初，官至浙江布政使。

translations.literal: His son Zhongji, at the beginning of Xuantong, reached the office of Zhejiang provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongji rose early in the Xuantong reign to provincial treasurer of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: =怡良=怡良，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Yi Liang, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Liang, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 刑部筆帖式，洊升員外郎。

translations.literal: He was a clerk in the Ministry of Justice and was repeatedly promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in the Ministry of Justice and rose step by step to vice director.

sentences.zh: 道光八年，出為廣東高州知府，調廣西南寧。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daoguang he went out as prefect of Gaozhou in Guangdong and was transferred to Nanning in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 8 he was posted as prefect of Gaozhou in Guangdong and then transferred to Nanning in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 歷雲南鹽法道，山東鹽運使，安徽、江蘇按察使，江西、江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Yunnan salt law intendant, Shandong salt transport commissioner, Anhui and Jiangsu provincial judicial commissioners, and Jiangxi and Jiangsu provincial treasurers.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Yunnan salt intendant, Shandong salt transport commissioner, judicial commissioner of Anhui and Jiangsu, and provincial treasurer of Jiangxi and Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Guangdong provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he was promoted to governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 禁煙事起，林則徐、鄧廷楨主之，怡良偕預其事。

translations.literal: When the opium prohibition affair arose, Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen took charge of it, and Yi Liang together took part in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the opium suppression campaign began, Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen led it, and Yi Liang took part with them.

sentences.zh: 二十年，兼署粵海關監督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he also acted as superintendent of the Guangdong maritime customs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he also served as acting superintendent of the Guangdong customs.

sentences.zh: 及琦善至，撤防議撫，疏請暫示羈縻，怡良及將軍阿精阿皆不列銜。

translations.literal: When Qishan arrived, defenses were withdrawn and peace was discussed; he memorialized requesting temporarily to show loose control; Yi Liang and General Ajing'a were both not listed in the joint signature.
translations.idiomatic: When Qishan arrived he pulled back the defenses and sought peace, memorializing for a temporary show of restraint. Yi Liang and General Ajing'a were not even named on the memorial.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月，沙角、大角砲台既失，琦善私許通商，並給香港，義律行文大鵬協撤回營汛。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year, after the Shajiao and Dajiao batteries were lost, Qishan privately permitted trade and also gave Hong Kong; Elliot sent documents to the Dapeng assistant commander ordering withdrawal of garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 21, after the Shajiao and Dajiao batteries fell, Qishan privately allowed trade and ceded Hong Kong. Elliot sent orders through the Dapeng assistant commander to withdraw the garrisons.

sentences.zh: 怡良疏陳曰：「自琦善到粵以後，辦理洋務，未經知會。

translations.literal: Yi Liang memorialized, saying: "Since Qishan arrived in Guangdong, in handling foreign affairs there has been no notification.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Liang memorialized: "Since Qishan reached Guangdong he has handled foreign affairs without informing us.

sentences.zh: 忽聞傳說義律已在香港出示，令民人歸順彼國。

translations.literal: Suddenly one hears the report that Elliot has already posted notices in Hong Kong ordering the people to submit to his country.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly we hear that Elliot has posted proclamations in Hong Kong ordering the people to submit to Britain.

sentences.zh: 提臣移諮副將鈔呈偽示，臣不勝駭異。

translations.literal: The provincial commander transferred a consultation to the deputy general with a copied false notice; your servant is overwhelmed with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial commander forwarded a copy of the spurious notice from the deputy general, and I am appalled beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 大西洋自前明寄居澳門，相沿已久，均歸中國同知、縣丞管轄，議者猶以為非計。

translations.literal: Westerners since the former Ming have sojourned at Macao, handed down for long; all are under the jurisdiction of China's subprefect and county aide, yet debaters still thought it an unwise plan.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners have lived at Macao since the Ming, and even that arrangement, under Chinese subprefects and county aides, was long criticized as unwise.

sentences.zh: 今英人竟佔踞全島，去虎門甚近，片帆可到。

translations.literal: Now the English have actually occupied the whole island; it is very close to Humen—a single sail can reach there.
translations.idiomatic: Now the British have seized the whole island, close enough to Humen that a single sail can reach it.

sentences.zh: 沿海之地，防不勝防，犯法之徒，必以為藏納之藪，地方因之不靖，法律有所不行。

translations.literal: Along the coast defenses cannot guard against everything; lawbreakers will surely take it as a hiding lair, the locality will thereby be unsettled, and law will in places not be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: The coast cannot be guarded everywhere. Criminals will treat it as a refuge, the region will grow restless, and the law will no longer reach everywhere it should.

sentences.zh: 更恐洋情反覆，要求不遂之時，仍以非禮相向，雖欲追悔，其何可及！

translations.literal: Further one fears foreign moods may turn; when demands are not met they may still treat us discourteously—though one wishes to repent afterward, how could one reach it!
translations.idiomatic: We must also fear that foreigners may turn capricious and, when their demands are refused, treat us discourteously again. By then repentance will come too late.

sentences.zh: 聖慮周詳，無遠不照，何待臣鰓鰓過計。

translations.literal: The sage's consideration is thorough and complete; nothing far is unillumined—why wait for your servant's gill-fluttering excessive plans?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's foresight is complete and reaches every distance. Why should I offer anxious, excessive warnings?

sentences.zh: 但忽聞海疆要地，外人公然主掌，天朝百姓，稱為英國之民，臣實不勝憤恨。

translations.literal: But suddenly hearing that a vital maritime place is openly ruled by foreigners, and that the Heavenly Dynasty's people are called subjects of England—your servant truly cannot overcome rage.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to hear suddenly that a vital maritime post is openly ruled by foreigners and that the emperor's people are called subjects of Britain fills me with unbearable anger.

sentences.zh: 一切駕馭機宜，臣無從悉其顛末。

translations.literal: As to all measures of control and timing, your servant has no way to know their beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: As for every measure of control and policy, I have no way to learn how matters began or where they stand.

sentences.zh: 惟上年十二月二十八日欽奉諭旨，調集兵丁，預備進剿，並令琦善同林則徐、鄧廷楨妥辦，均經宣示。

translations.literal: Only on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month of last year an imperial edict was received ordering troops gathered and prepared for advance and punitive attack, and commanding Qishan together with Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen to handle matters properly—all had been proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Only last year, on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month, we received an imperial edict to gather troops for a punitive advance and to have Qishan work with Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen to settle affairs properly. That order was proclaimed to all.

sentences.zh: 臣等請添募兵勇，固守虎門，防堵要隘。

translations.literal: Your servants requested adding recruited braves, firmly holding Humen, and blocking vital passes.
translations.idiomatic: We asked to recruit more troops, hold Humen firmly, and block the vital passes.

sentences.zh: 今英人窺伺多端，實有措手莫及之勢。

translations.literal: Now the English spy and watch in many ways; there truly is a situation where one cannot lay hands in time.
translations.idiomatic: Now the British watch us from many angles, and the situation has truly grown beyond our reach.

sentences.zh: 不敢緘默，謹以上聞。」

translations.literal: Not daring to keep silent, I respectfully report the above."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not keep silent and respectfully report this to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 於是詔斥琦善專擅之罪，褫職逮治，怡良兼署總督。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict rebuked Qishan's crime of acting on his own authority, stripped his office and ordered arrest; Yi Liang also acted as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: The court then rebuked Qishan for acting on his own authority, stripped him of office, and ordered his arrest. Yi Liang was made acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 英兵尋陷虎門，命怡良會同參贊大臣楊芳進剿，合疏請許英屬港腳商船貿易，詔斥怠慢軍心，奪職留任。

translations.literal: English troops soon took Humen; Yi Liang was ordered together with Grand Minister Consultant Yang Fang to advance and attack; jointly they memorialized requesting permission for English-subject port-foot merchant ships to trade; an edict rebuked slackening army morale, stripped office but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: British forces soon took Humen. Yi Liang was ordered to advance with Grand Minister Consultant Yang Fang, but together they asked permission for British merchant shipping to trade. The court rebuked them for weakening morale, stripped their ranks, yet kept them in office.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，授欽差大臣，會辦福建軍務，署閩浙總督，尋實授。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed Imperial Commissioner to jointly handle Fujian military affairs, acted as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he became Imperial Commissioner for Fujian military affairs, served as acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, and soon received the substantive post.

sentences.zh: 時英兵已去廈門，其留泊鼓浪嶼者僅數艘。

translations.literal: At that time English troops had already left Xiamen; those remaining anchored at Gulangyu were only several ships.
translations.idiomatic: By then the British had left Xiamen, and only a few ships remained at Gulangyu.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，福州、廈門皆開口岸，命偕巡撫劉鴻翱議善後事宜，籌辦通商，兼署福州將軍。

translations.literal: When the peace agreement was made, Fuzhou and Xiamen both opened treaty ports; he was ordered together with Governor Liu Hong'ao to discuss postwar arrangements, arrange trade, and also act as Fuzhou regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was concluded Fuzhou and Xiamen were opened as treaty ports. He was ordered with Governor Liu Hong'ao to settle postwar affairs, organize trade, and also serve as acting commander at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是台灣鎮、道禦敵，迭有擒斬，英人追訴其妄殺冒功，命怡良渡台灣查辦，總兵達洪阿、道員姚瑩逮京。

translations.literal: Earlier the Taiwan garrison commander and circuit intendant in resisting the enemy had repeatedly captured and beheaded foes; the English pursued complaint that they had killed rashly and falsely claimed merit; Yi Liang was ordered to cross to Taiwan to investigate; Regional Commander Da Hong'a and Circuit Intendant Yao Ying were escorted to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Taiwan commander and intendant had won repeated captures and killings in battle. The British complained of false kills and bogus merit claims, and Yi Liang was sent to Taiwan to investigate. Regional Commander Da Hong'a and Circuit Intendant Yao Ying were brought to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 當和議初定，怡良不能為之剖雪，為時論所譏。

translations.literal: When the peace agreement was first settled, Yi Liang could not clear them of blame and was ridiculed by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was first concluded Yi Liang failed to clear their names, and public opinion mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he requested leave for illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he asked to retire on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，起授福州將軍，偕協辦大學士杜受田治山東賑務。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was recalled and appointed Fuzhou regional commander, and together with Associate Grand Secretary Du Shoutian managed Shandong relief affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 he was recalled as regional commander at Fuzhou and, with Associate Grand Secretary Du Shoutian, directed famine relief in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 三年，授兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 江寧、鎮江已陷，暫駐常州。

translations.literal: Jiangning and Zhenjiang had already fallen; he temporarily stationed himself at Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning and Zhenjiang had already fallen, so he made his temporary headquarters at Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 粵匪方熾，兵事由欽差大臣琦善、向榮主之，分駐大江南北。

translations.literal: Guangdong bandits were then raging; military affairs were led by Imperial Commissioners Qishan and Xiang Rong, stationed separately north and south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong rebels were raging, and military affairs were led by Imperial Commissioners Qishan and Xiang Rong, who were posted on opposite sides of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 上海逆匪劉麗川踞城，連陷川沙、青浦、南匯、嘉定、寶山。

translations.literal: The Shanghai rebel Liu Lichuan held the city and in succession took Chuansha, Qingpu, Nanhui, Jiading, and Baoshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanghai rebel Liu Lichuan seized the city and in quick succession overran Chuansha, Qingpu, Nanhui, Jiading, and Baoshan.

sentences.zh: 麗川，粵人，商於滬。

translations.literal: Lichuan was a Cantonese who traded at Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Lichuan was a Cantonese merchant in Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 初起，冒用洋行公司鈐記出示，眾論洶洶，疑有通洋情事。

translations.literal: At the first rise he falsely used the seal of a foreign firm to issue notices; public talk was turbulent, suspecting dealings with foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset he issued proclamations under a foreign firm's seal, and rumor swirled that he was in league with foreigners.

sentences.zh: 怡良疏請閩、浙、江西絲茶暫行停運，使洋商失自然之利，急望克復，自能嚴斷濟賊。

translations.literal: Yi Liang memorialized requesting that Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi silk and tea temporarily cease transport, so foreign merchants would lose their natural profit, urgently hope for recovery, and of themselves could strictly cut off aid to bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Liang asked that silk and tea shipments from Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi be halted for a time so foreign merchants would lose their profits, press for the city's recovery, and themselves cut off aid to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 巡撫吉爾杭阿率兵進剿，逾年乃平。

translations.literal: Governor Ji'erhang'a led troops to advance and suppress; after more than a year it was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ji'erhang'a led the campaign to suppress them, and the rising was not put down until more than a year later.

sentences.zh: 時各國因在廣東爭入城，與總督葉名琛齟齬，每赴上海有所陳議，諭怡良隨時妥辦，勿徇要求。

translations.literal: At that time the various countries, because of disputing entry into the city at Guangdong with Governor-General Ye Mingchen, each went to Shanghai to make representations; Yi Liang was instructed to handle matters properly at all times and not indulge demands.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign powers were then quarreling with Governor-General Ye Mingchen over entry into Guangzhou and often brought their petitions to Shanghai. Yi Liang was told to handle each case properly and not yield to their demands.

sentences.zh: 五年，粵匪攻金壇，遣總兵傅振邦、虎嵩林會西安將軍福興、漳州鎮總兵張國樑進剿，連捷，解圍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Guangdong bandits attacked Jintan; he dispatched Regional Commanders Fu Zhenbang and Hu Songlin to join Xi'an General Fuxing and Zhang Guoliang, regional commander of Zhangzhou garrison, to advance and suppress; they won successive victories and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Guangdong rebels attacked Jintan. He sent Regional Commanders Fu Zhenbang and Hu Songlin to join with Xi'an General Fuxing and Zhangzhou Commander Zhang Guoliang. They won repeated victories and raised the siege.

sentences.zh: 國樑進克東壩，福興與之不洽，詔怡良密察以聞。

translations.literal: Guoliang advanced and took Dongba; Fuxing was not in harmony with him; an edict ordered Yi Liang secretly to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang advanced and took Dongba, but he and Fuxing were at odds. The court ordered Yi Liang to investigate quietly and report back.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「國樑勇戰，福興所不及，人皆重張輕福。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Guoliang fights bravely, which Fuxing cannot match; everyone esteems Zhang and looks lightly on Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Guoliang fights bravely as Fuxing cannot, and everyone esteems Zhang while slighting Fu.

sentences.zh: 因有芥蒂，請分調以免貽誤。」

translations.literal: Because there is ill feeling between them, I request they be transferred separately to avoid causing harm."
translations.idiomatic: Because they bear a grudge against each other, I ask that they be posted apart so the campaign is not harmed."

sentences.zh: 尋命福興赴江西勦賊。

translations.literal: Soon Fuxing was ordered to Jiangxi to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxing was soon ordered to Jiangxi to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 大軍圍江寧，久無功，賊勢益蔓。

translations.literal: The great army besieged Jiangning for long without success, and the bandit power spread ever more.
translations.idiomatic: The main force besieged Jiangning for a long time without success, and the rebels spread ever wider.

sentences.zh: 七年，以病請解，允之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he requested relief on grounds of illness and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he asked to be relieved on grounds of illness, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: =祁𡎴=祁𡎴，字竹軒，山西高平人。

translations.literal: Qi Jun, style name Zhuxuan, was a native of Gaoping in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jun, whose style was Zhuxuan, came from Gaoping in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年進士，授刑部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the first year of Jiaqing, he was appointed director in the Ministry of Justice and was transferred to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in Jiaqing 1, entered the Ministry of Justice as a director, and was later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 督廣西學政，任滿補原官。

translations.literal: He supervised Guangxi educational administration; when his term ended he returned to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational commissioner of Guangxi and, when his term ended, returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 以承審宗室敏學獄不實，褫職。

translations.literal: Because in presiding over the case of the imperial clansman Minxue he was not factual, his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for mishandling the trial of the imperial clansman Minxue.

sentences.zh: 尋予刑部七品小京官，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was given a seventh-rank minor Beijing official post in the Ministry of Justice and was repeatedly promoted to director of a bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given a seventh-rank post in the Ministry of Justice and rose step by step to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，出為河南糧鹽道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang he went out as Henan grain-and-salt intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 4 he was posted as Henan grain-and-salt intendant.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江按察使，覆檢德清徐倪氏獄，得官吏受賄蒙蔽狀，尚書王鼎覆訊，如𡎴議。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhejiang provincial judicial commissioner; reexamining the Deqing Xu-Ni clan case, he obtained the situation of officials receiving bribes and covering up; Minister Wang Ding re-investigated and followed Jun's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He became judicial commissioner of Zhejiang and reopened the Deqing Xu-Ni clan case, uncovering officials who had taken bribes and concealed the truth. Minister Wang Ding reviewed the case and upheld Jun's findings.

sentences.zh: 遷貴州布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guizhou provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to provincial treasurer of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，召授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned and appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was recalled to the capital and appointed vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 尋出為廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Guangxi provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十二年，湖南、廣東瑤匪並起，𡎴遣兵防富川、恭城、賀縣，搜捕竄匪，追擊於芳林渡，斬擒千餘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Yao bandits rose together in Hunan and Guangdong; Jun dispatched troops to guard Fuchuan, Gongcheng, and Hexian, searched and captured fleeing bandits, pursued at Fanglin Ford, and beheaded or captured more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 Yao rebels rose in both Hunan and Guangdong. Jun sent troops to guard Fuchuan, Gongcheng, and Hexian, hunted down fugitives, pursued them at Fanglin Ford, and killed or captured more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 瑤平，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When the Yao were pacified he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yao were pacified he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 疏陳善後策，扼要移駐文武，稽查化導，如所議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized post-pacification measures: moving civil and military officials to key points, inspecting and guiding transformation—and it was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on postwar measures, proposing to station civil and military officials at key points and to inspect and guide local reform. His plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 十三年，調廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Guangdong provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was transferred to governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時盧坤為總督，和衷撫馭，籌修海防。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Kun was governor-general; in harmony they governed and soothed, and planned coastal defense repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lu Kun was then in office. They worked in harmony to govern the province and plan coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 十五年，代坤兼署總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he replaced Kun and also acted as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he replaced Lu Kun and also served as acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十八年，召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was summoned as minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he was recalled to serve as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 宣宗知𡎴習練法律，故有此授。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor knew Jun was practiced in law, and therefore made this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor knew Jun's mastery of law and gave him the post for that reason.

sentences.zh: 京察，被議敘。

translations.literal: At the capital inspection he was subject to deliberated ranking.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital inspection his performance was formally rated.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，靖逆將軍奕山督師廣東，命𡎴往治餉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Pacification General Yishan commanded troops in Guangdong and ordered Jun to go manage pay supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 Pacification General Yishan took command in Guangdong and sent Jun to manage supplies.

sentences.zh: 琦善既黜，授兩廣總督。

translations.literal: After Qishan was dismissed, Jun was appointed governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: After Qishan was dismissed, Jun was appointed governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時英兵踞虎門，省城遷避過半，𡎴示以鎮靜，稍稍安集。

translations.literal: At that time English troops held Humen; more than half the provincial city had moved away in flight; Jun showed calm, and little by little people settled.
translations.idiomatic: British troops then held Humen, and more than half the provincial capital had fled. Jun projected calm, and the population slowly returned.

sentences.zh: 參贊大臣楊芳主持重勿浪戰，奕山為其下所慫恿，商之𡎴。

translations.literal: Grand Minister Consultant Yang Fang upheld the importance of not fighting rashly; Yishan was egged on by his subordinates and consulted Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister Consultant Yang Fang urged caution against reckless fighting. Yishan was urged on by his staff and consulted Jun.

sentences.zh: 𡎴以敵方恣哃喝，大軍新至，乘銳而用，冀挫其焰，未阻止，遂突攻英艦於省河，敵猝未備，義律夜遁。

translations.literal: Jun, because the enemy was wantonly shouting abuse, and the great army had newly arrived, urged using their sharpness to hope to blunt the enemy's flame; he did not stop them, and they suddenly attacked English ships on the provincial river; the enemy was suddenly unprepared, and Elliot fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued that the enemy were swaggering and that the newly arrived main force should strike while morale was high to break their momentum. He failed to stop the attack on British ships in the provincial river. The enemy were caught unprepared, and Elliot fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 遲明，英兵大至，逼砲台，守兵潰，英兵進踞城北耆定台，高瞰城中。

translations.literal: At daybreak English troops came in force, pressed the batteries, defenders fled, English troops advanced and held Qiding Terrace north of the city, looking down on the city from above.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn a large British force arrived, pressed the batteries, and routed the defenders. They seized Qiding Terrace north of the city and looked down on Guangzhou from above.

sentences.zh: 𡎴與巡撫怡良亟守西南兩門，城外市屋盡毀，客兵皆撤入城。

translations.literal: Jun and Governor Yi Liang urgently held the southwest two gates; market houses outside the city were all destroyed, and guest troops were all withdrawn into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Governor Yi Liang rushed to hold the southwest gates. The markets outside the walls were wrecked, and all outside troops were pulled back into the city.

sentences.zh: 商民知兵不足恃，環請為目前計，款議遂決，予洋銀六百萬元。

translations.literal: Merchants and people, knowing troops could not be relied on, surrounded them requesting a plan for the present moment; peace talks were then decided, and six million dollars in foreign silver were given.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and townspeople, seeing that the army could not be trusted, pressed for an immediate settlement. Peace talks were agreed and six million dollars in foreign silver were paid.

sentences.zh: 英艦退出虎門，而耆定台兵未去，船泊泥城，登岸侵擾，其兵目伯麥闖入三元里，民憤，磔之。

translations.literal: English ships withdrew from Humen, but troops on Qiding Terrace did not leave; ships anchored at Nicheng, landed and harassed; their officer Burkill broke into Sanyuanli; the people were enraged and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: British ships withdrew from Humen, but troops remained on Qiding Terrace. Others anchored at Nicheng and raided ashore. Officer Burkill entered Sanyuanli, and enraged villagers killed and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 義律馳救，受圍，遣廣州知府餘保純護之出，令率眾盡退虎門外。

translations.literal: Elliot rushed to rescue, was surrounded, sent Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun to escort him out, and ordered him to lead the crowd to withdraw entirely outside Humen.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot rushed to rescue his men but was surrounded. He sent Prefect Yu Baochun to escort him out and ordered the crowd to withdraw entirely beyond Humen.

sentences.zh: 於是鄉團日盛，紳士黃培芳、餘廷槐等合南海、番禺諸鄉立七社，萬人一呼而集儲穀十餘萬石，不動官帑。

translations.literal: Thereupon village militia grew daily; gentry Huang Peifang, Yu Tinghuai, and others joined villages of Nanhai and Panyu to establish seven societies; ten thousand men answered one call and gathered, storing more than a hundred thousand shi of grain without touching official funds.
translations.idiomatic: Village militia then flourished. Gentry such as Huang Peifang and Yu Tinghuai united villages in Nanhai and Panyu into seven societies. Ten thousand men could be summoned at a call, and they stored more than a hundred thousand shi of grain without touching public funds.

sentences.zh: 𡎴用林則徐堵塞省河之法，以資守禦。

translations.literal: Jun used Lin Zexu's method of blocking the provincial river to support defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jun adopted Lin Zexu's method of blocking the provincial river to strengthen the defenses.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，英人交還虎門砲台，偕奕山疏陳：「現練水陸義勇三萬六千餘名，並各鄉丁壯，分成團練。

translations.literal: That summer the English returned the Humen batteries; together with Yishan he memorialized: "At present land and water volunteers trained number more than thirty-six thousand, together with able men of each village, divided into militia training.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the British returned the Humen batteries. Jun and Yishan reported: "We now have more than thirty-six thousand trained land and water volunteers, together with able men from the villages organized as militia.

sentences.zh: 前調各省官兵，遵旨陸續分撤。」

translations.literal: Troops earlier transferred from each province, following the edict, are being withdrawn in succession."
translations.idiomatic: The troops earlier transferred from other provinces are being withdrawn in succession as ordered."

sentences.zh: 詔促規复香港，責𡎴與奕山各抒所見。

translations.literal: An edict urged planning recovery of Hong Kong and charged Jun and Yishan each to set forth his views.
translations.idiomatic: The court urged plans to recover Hong Kong and ordered Jun and Yishan each to submit his views.

sentences.zh: 𡎴奏：「欲收復香港，必先修虎門砲台，然非設險省河，虎門亦難興工。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized: "To wish to recover Hong Kong, one must first repair the Humen batteries; yet unless defenses are set on the provincial river, Humen also will be hard to start work on.
translations.idiomatic: Jun wrote: "To recover Hong Kong we must first repair the Humen batteries, but work at Humen cannot begin until the provincial river is fortified.

sentences.zh: 先於獅子洋、蚺蛇洞諸要隘築堡守戍。」

translations.literal: First at vital passes such as the Lion Sea and Python Cave build forts and garrison them."
translations.idiomatic: Forts should first be built and garrisoned at key points such as the Lion Sea and Python Cave."

sentences.zh: 疏上，報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial went up and acknowledgment was reported.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 是時粵師實無力進剿，英人既得賂而去，兵勢趨重江、浙，得以苟安。

translations.literal: At that time Guangdong forces truly had no strength to advance and suppress; the English, having received bribes, departed, and military momentum shifted heavily to Jiangsu and Zhejiang, so they could barely rest secure.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong forces then had no real strength to take the offensive. Once the British took their payment and left, the war shifted to Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and the province settled into an uneasy peace.

sentences.zh: 奕山屢被嚴詰，麾下招誘海盜，獻計襲攻敵艦，奕山又為所動，𡎴勸寢其議。

translations.literal: Yishan was repeatedly severely questioned; under him pirates were recruited and tempted, offering plans to raid enemy ships; Yishan was again moved by them, and Jun urged abandoning the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan was repeatedly rebuked by the court. His staff recruited pirates who offered plans to attack enemy ships, and Yishan was swayed until Jun persuaded him to drop the idea.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，和議成，英商開市益驕，民怨益深，焚其館，擲貨於衢，濮鼎查責言，𡎴撫慰之，得無事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the peace agreement was made; English merchants trading at the opened market grew ever more arrogant, popular resentment deepened, their halls were burned and goods thrown into the streets; Pottinger lodged complaints; Jun soothed them and there was no incident.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 peace was concluded. British merchants at the opened markets grew arrogant, popular anger deepened, their warehouses were burned and goods thrown into the streets. Pottinger protested, but Jun calmed matters and prevented a crisis.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，虎門砲台工竣，疏言：「舊式砲台僅可禦海盜，今仿洋法，以三合土築人字形，砲牆量宜增移改建。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year work on the Humen batteries was completed; he memorialized: "Old-style batteries can only repel pirates; now imitating foreign methods, build in rammed earth in human character form; battery walls should suitably be increased, moved, and rebuilt."
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 the Humen batteries were finished. He reported that the old forts could repel only pirates and that new works should follow foreign methods, with rammed-earth batteries in chevron form and walls rebuilt to proper scale."

sentences.zh: 又請就海壖圍沙成田一百六十餘頃，可給屯丁二千人，且耕且守防要隘。

translations.literal: He also requested enclosing sand along the seashore to form fields of more than 160 qing, which could supply two thousand garrison colonists who would both farm and guard vital passes.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to reclaim coastal sand into more than 160 qing of fields to support two thousand garrison colonists who would farm while guarding the vital passes.

sentences.zh: 並陳粵民義奮、團練可用狀，諭責事期經久，俾濟實用。

translations.literal: He also set forth the situation of Guangdong people's righteous zeal and usable militia training; an edict rebuked that affairs must be long-lasting to be of practical use.
translations.idiomatic: He also described the zeal of Guangdong people and the usefulness of militia training. The court replied that such measures must be sustained over time if they were to be truly useful.

sentences.zh: 以病乞休，累疏乃得請。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested retirement; only after repeated memorials was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of illness and was granted leave only after repeated memorials.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒，優詔依尚書例賜卹，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died; a favorable edict followed the minister precedent in granting condolence payments; posthumous title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 24. The court granted condolence payments according to the precedent for a minister and gave him the posthumous title Wenge.

sentences.zh: =黃恩彤=黃恩彤，字石琴，山東寧陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Entong, style name Shiqin, was a native of Ningyang in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Entong, whose style was Shiqin, came from Ningyang in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光六年進士，授刑部主事，治獄數有平反。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the sixth year of Daoguang, he was appointed director in the Ministry of Justice; in handling cases he several times secured reversals.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in Daoguang 6 and entered the Ministry of Justice as a director, winning several reversals in criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 充提牢，以疏防越獄降調，尋復之。

translations.literal: He served as prison superintendent; for lax guard allowing escape he was demoted and transferred, but soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: As prison superintendent he was demoted when a prisoner escaped through lax security, but was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 充熱河理刑司員，卻翁牛特蒙古公賄，黜其爵。

translations.literal: He served as a Rehe judicial bureau officer; he refused a bribe from the Mongol prince of Ujimqin and stripped him of his rank.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Rehe judicial bureau he refused a bribe from the Ujimqin Mongol prince and stripped him of his title.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 二十年，出為江南鹽巡道，遷按察使，署江寧布政使。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he went out as Jiangnan salt patrol intendant, was transferred to provincial judicial commissioner, and acted as Jiangning provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was posted as Jiangnan salt patrol intendant, became judicial commissioner, and served as acting treasurer at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 英兵犯江寧，耆英、伊里布令恩彤偕侍衛咸齡赴敵艦議款，隨同定約。

translations.literal: When English troops attacked Jiangning, Qiying and Yilibu ordered Entong together with Bodyguard Xianling to go to enemy ships to discuss terms and together fixed the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: When British forces attacked Jiangning, Qiying and Yilibu sent Entong with Bodyguard Xianling to the enemy ships to negotiate terms and conclude the treaty.

sentences.zh: 事竣，复隨伊里布赴廣東，籌議通商。

translations.literal: When affairs were concluded he again followed Yilibu to Guangdong to plan trade arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: When that business was finished he went with Yilibu to Guangdong to organize trade.

sentences.zh: 改番舶互市歸官辦，增減稅則，稽查偷漏，悉由恩彤與粵海關監督文豐商定。

translations.literal: Changing foreign-ship mutual trade to official management, increasing or reducing tax rules, and inspecting smuggling and leakage—all were settled by Entong together with Guangdong customs superintendent Wen Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Placing foreign trade under official management, revising the tax schedule, and inspecting smuggling were all arranged by Entong with Customs Superintendent Wen Feng.

sentences.zh: 調廣東按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangdong provincial judicial commissioner and promoted to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to judicial commissioner of Guangdong and then promoted to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 美利堅人顧盛請入京，恩彤赴澳門辯折，止其行，賜花翎。

translations.literal: The American Cushing requested entry into the capital; Entong went to Macao to argue and dissuade, stopping his journey, and was given a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When the American diplomat Cushing sought entry to Beijing, Entong went to Macao to argue him out of it and was rewarded with a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted on the spot to provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he was promoted directly to provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 恩彤疏陳洋務，略曰：「欲靖外侮，先防內變。

translations.literal: Entong memorialized on foreign affairs, saying in summary: "To pacify external insult, first guard against internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Entong memorialized on foreign affairs, writing in part: "To end foreign aggression we must first guard against internal disorder.

sentences.zh: 粵民性情剽悍，難與爭鋒，亦難與持久。

translations.literal: Guangdong people's nature is fierce and hard to meet in contest of arms, and also hard to keep in prolonged struggle.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong are fierce by nature. They are hard to match in a sudden clash and harder still to keep in a long fight.

sentences.zh: 未可因三元里一戰，遽信為民足禦侮也。

translations.literal: One cannot because of one battle at Sanyuanli hastily believe the people are sufficient to resist insult.
translations.idiomatic: We must not believe from the fight at Sanyuanli alone that the people are enough to repel foreign aggression.

sentences.zh: 該夷現雖釋怨就撫，而一切駕馭之方與防備之具，不可一日不講。

translations.literal: Those barbarians now though releasing resentment and submitting to pacification, all methods of control and means of defense cannot for one day go undiscussed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the foreigners have for now laid aside their grievances and accepted pacification, methods of control and means of defense must be discussed every day.

sentences.zh: 但當示以恩信，妥為羈縻，一面慎固海防，簡練軍實。

translations.literal: One should only show them favor and trust, properly keep them on loose reins, and on one side carefully strengthen coastal defense and streamline military substance.
translations.idiomatic: We should show them favor and trust and keep them on a loose rein, while at the same time strengthening coastal defenses and streamlining the army.

sentences.zh: 尤必撫柔我民，所欲與聚，所惡勿施，以固人心而維邦本。

translations.literal: Especially one must soothe our people—give what they desire and gather it, do not impose what they hate—to solidify popular hearts and maintain the state's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Above all we must win over our own people, giving them what they desire and withholding what they hate, so as to secure popular loyalty and the foundation of the state.

sentences.zh: 庶在我有隱然之威，因以折彼囂凌之氣。」

translations.literal: Then perhaps we would have a hidden authority, and thereby break their arrogant bullying spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Then we may possess a quiet authority that will in turn curb their arrogance."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上韙之。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and the emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋屆京察，與耆英並被議敘。

translations.literal: Soon the capital inspection came due, and he together with Qiying were both subject to deliberated ranking.
translations.idiomatic: At the next capital inspection he and Qiying were both formally rated.

sentences.zh: 籌備海防，裁虎門屯丁，以沙田租稅充戰船砲台歲修之費。

translations.literal: He planned coastal defense preparations, cut Humen garrison colonists, and used sand-field rent taxes to cover annual repair costs for war junks and batteries.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared coastal defenses, reduced the Humen garrison colonists, and funded annual repairs to warships and batteries from sand-field rents.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，英人爭入城，議久不決，粵民憤不可諭，恩彤前疏不為時論所與，被劾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the English disputed entry into the city; deliberation long went unresolved; Guangdong people's anger could not be instructed away; Entong's earlier memorial was not joined by contemporary opinion, and he was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 the British pressed to enter the city. Talks dragged on, Cantonese anger could not be calmed, and Entong's earlier cautious memorial won no support. He was impeached.

sentences.zh: 會監臨文武鄉試，疏請年老武生給予武職虛銜，詔斥其違例，褫職，交耆英差遣。

translations.literal: When supervising the civil and military provincial examinations he memorialized requesting that elderly military licentiates be given nominal military ranks; an edict rebuked this as violating regulations, stripped his office, and handed him to Qiying for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the provincial examinations he asked that elderly military licentiates receive nominal military titles. The court rebuked this as irregular, stripped his office, and placed him under Qiying's orders.

sentences.zh: 尋以同知銓選。

translations.literal: Soon he was selected by examination for subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed subprefect through regular selection.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，告養歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he reported for retirement to care for parents and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he retired to care for his parents and returned home.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，在籍治團練。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, while at home he managed militia training.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he organized local militia at home.

sentences.zh: 天津議和，命隨耆英往，恩彤至，則款議已定，仍請終養，同治中，以御捻匪功，予三品封典。

translations.literal: When peace was negotiated at Tianjin he was ordered to follow Qiying; when Entong arrived the peace talks were already settled; he still requested to finish caring for parents; in the Tongzhi period, for merit in resisting the Nian bandits, he was given third-rank ennoblement privileges.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was negotiated at Tianjin he was ordered to accompany Qiying, but by the time he arrived the treaty was already settled. He again asked to finish caring for his parents. In the Tongzhi era he earned third-rank ennoblement privileges for fighting the Nian rebels.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，鄉舉重逢，加二品銜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu, meeting again the provincial examination anniversary, he was given second-rank button.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 7, on the anniversary of his provincial examination, he was given second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: =劉韻珂=劉韻珂，字玉坡，山東汶上人。

translations.literal: Liu Yunke, style name Yupou, was a native of Wenshang in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yunke, whose style was Yupou, came from Wenshang in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 由拔貢授刑部七品小京官，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: From presented tribute student he was appointed a seventh-rank minor Beijing official in the Ministry of Justice and was repeatedly promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the tribute student examination he entered the Ministry of Justice as a seventh-rank official and rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 道光八年，出為安徽徽州知府，調安慶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daoguang he went out as prefect of Huizhou in Anhui and was transferred to Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 8 he was posted as prefect of Huizhou in Anhui and then transferred to Anqing.

sentences.zh: 歷雲南鹽法道，浙江、廣西按察使，四川布政使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Yunnan salt law intendant, Zhejiang and Guangxi provincial judicial commissioners, and Sichuan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Yunnan salt intendant, judicial commissioner of Zhejiang and Guangxi, and provincial treasurer of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Zhejiang provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was promoted to governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 定海已陷，韻珂於寧波收撫難民。

translations.literal: Dinghai had already fallen; Yunke at Ningbo received and soothed refugees.
translations.idiomatic: After Dinghai fell, Yunke received and cared for refugees at Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 沿海設防，欽差大臣伊里布駐鎮海督師，琦善方議以香港易還定海，韻珂疏言：「定海為通洋適中之地，英人已築砲台、開河道，經營一切。

translations.literal: Coastal defenses were set; Imperial Commissioner Yilibu stationed at Zhenhai to command troops; Qishan was then discussing exchanging Hong Kong to recover Dinghai; Yunke memorialized: "Dinghai is a place midway suitable for reaching the ocean; the English have already built batteries, opened waterways, and managed everything.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal defenses were organized while Imperial Commissioner Yilibu commanded at Zhenhai. Qishan was discussing trading Hong Kong for Dinghai. Yunke wrote: "Dinghai lies at a central point on the sea routes. The British have already built batteries, opened waterways, and developed the place fully.

sentences.zh: 彼或餌漁、盜為羽翼，其患非小。

translations.literal: They may bait fishermen and pirates as wings—the harm is not small.
translations.idiomatic: They may win over fishermen and pirates as allies, and the danger would be grave.

sentences.zh: 浙江為財賦之區，寧波又為浙省菁華所在，宜預杜覬覦。」

translations.literal: Zhejiang is a region of wealth and grain supply; Ningbo is again where Zhejiang's finest resources lie—one should beforehand block covetous eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang is a rich province, and Ningbo holds its finest resources. We should forestall any covetous designs."

sentences.zh: 尋詔斥伊里布附和琦善，罷去，以裕謙代之，命韻珂偕提督余步雲治鎮海防務。

translations.literal: Soon an edict rebuked Yilibu for echoing Qishan, dismissed him, replaced him with Yijing, and ordered Yunke together with Provincial Commander Yu Buyun to manage Zhenhai defense affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon rebuked Yilibu for siding with Qishan and dismissed him, replacing him with Yijing. Yunke was ordered to manage Zhenhai defenses with Provincial Commander Yu Buyun.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，英兵退出定海，仍遊奕浙洋，裕謙督師赴剿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year English troops withdrew from Dinghai but still roamed Zhejiang waters; Yijing commanded troops to advance and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 British troops left Dinghai but still ranged the Zhejiang coast. Yijing took command to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 定海再陷，鎮海、寧波相繼失守，裕謙死之。

translations.literal: Dinghai fell again; Zhenhai and Ningbo in succession were lost; Yijing died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai fell again, then Zhenhai and Ningbo in succession. Yijing died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 韻珂檄在籍布政使鄭祖琛率師扼曹娥江，總兵李廷揚、按察使蔣文慶、道員鹿澤良駐防紹興，募勇二萬人守省城，庀守具，清內奸，撫沙匪十麻子投誠效用，人心以安。

translations.literal: Yunke ordered the home-domiciled provincial treasurer Zheng Zuchen to lead troops to block the Cao'e River; Regional Commander Li Tingyang, Judicial Commissioner Jiang Wenqing, and Circuit Intendant Lu Zeliang garrisoned Shaoxing; he recruited twenty thousand braves to guard the provincial city, prepared defense equipment, cleared internal traitors, soothed the sand-bandit Shimazi into submission for service, and popular hearts thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yunke ordered home-domiciled Treasurer Zheng Zuchen to block the Cao'e River. Regional Commander Li Tingyang, Judicial Commissioner Jiang Wenqing, and Circuit Intendant Lu Zeliang held Shaoxing. He recruited twenty thousand militia to defend the provincial capital, prepared defenses, rooted out collaborators, won over the sand-bandit Shimazi, and steadied public morale.

sentences.zh: 英艦窺錢塘江，尋退去。

translations.literal: English ships spied on the Qiantang River, then soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: British ships probed the Qiantang River but soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 揚威將軍奕經援浙。

translations.literal: Campaign General Yijing came to aid Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign General Yijing arrived to reinforce Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，規復寧波，不克，擾及奉化、慈谿，戰數不利，命韻珂偕欽差大臣耆英籌辦防務。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year they planned to recover Ningbo but could not; disturbances reached Fenghua and Cixi; battles were several times unfavorable; Yunke was ordered together with Imperial Commissioner Qiying to plan defense affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 22 they tried to recover Ningbo but failed. Fighting spread to Fenghua and Cixi with repeated defeats. Yunke was ordered to plan defenses with Imperial Commissioner Qiying.

sentences.zh: 韻珂疏言：「浙事有十可慮，皆必然之患，無可解之憂，若不早為籌畫，國家大事豈容屢誤？

translations.literal: Yunke memorialized: "Zhejiang affairs have ten matters worth worrying over—all are inevitable troubles, worries without remedy; if one does not early make plans, can great affairs of state tolerate repeated errors?
translations.idiomatic: Yunke wrote: "There are ten grave worries in Zhejiang, each an inevitable danger with no easy remedy. If we do not plan early, how can the state afford repeated mistakes?

sentences.zh: 現在奕經赴海寧查看海口，文蔚留駐紹興調置前路防​​守，究竟此後作何籌辦，奕經等亦無定見。

translations.literal: Now Yijing has gone to Haining to inspect the sea mouth; Wenwei remains stationed at Shaoxing arranging forward defenses—after all, what planning is to be made hereafter, Yijing and the others also have no fixed view.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing has gone to Haining to inspect the harbor mouth while Wenwei stays at Shaoxing arranging the forward defenses. Even they have no settled plan for what comes next.

sentences.zh: 臣若不直陳，後日倘省垣不守，粉身碎骨，難蓋前愆。

translations.literal: If your servant does not speak plainly, later if the provincial capital cannot be held, though body be ground to powder and bones shattered, it would be hard to cover former fault.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not speak plainly now and the provincial capital later falls, no punishment will be enough to atone for my earlier failure.

sentences.zh: 伏乞俯念浙省危急，獨操乾斷，飭令將軍等隨機應變，俾浙省危而復安，天下胥受其福。」

translations.literal: I prostrate and beg you to bend mind to Zhejiang's peril, alone wield decisive judgment, order the generals and others to respond according to circumstance, so that Zhejiang from peril may return to peace and all under Heaven receive its blessing."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider Zhejiang's peril, decide alone with firm authority, and order the generals to act as circumstances require, so that Zhejiang may recover and the empire share the benefit."

sentences.zh: 又力荐伊里布「不貪功、不好名，為洋人所感戴。

translations.literal: He also strongly recommended Yilibu as "not greedy for merit, not fond of fame, and regarded with gratitude by foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: He also strongly recommended Yilibu as "free of ambition for merit or fame and respected by the foreigners.

sentences.zh: 其家人張喜亦可用。

translations.literal: His household member Zhang Xi is also usable.
translations.idiomatic: His servant Zhang Xi is also useful.

sentences.zh: 儻令來浙，或英兵不復內犯。」

translations.literal: If he were ordered to come to Zhejiang, perhaps English troops would not again invade inland."
translations.idiomatic: If he were sent to Zhejiang, the British might not invade inland again."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上頗採其言，命伊里布隨耆英赴浙，相機辦理。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and the emperor largely adopted his words, ordering Yilibu to follow Qiying to Zhejiang and handle matters as circumstances allowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely accepted his advice and ordered Yilibu to follow Qiying to Zhejiang and act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 四月，乍浦陷，伊里布往說英人退兵，於是改犯吳淞，入大江，乃於江寧定和議。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Zhapu fell; Yilibu went to persuade the English to withdraw troops; they then changed to attack Wusong, entered the great river, and thus at Jiangning fixed the peace agreement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhapu fell. Yilibu went to persuade the British to withdraw, but they turned instead to Wusong, entered the Yangzi, and concluded peace at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 韻珂貽書耆英、伊里布等曰：「撫局既定，後患頗多，有不能不鰓鰓過慮者。

translations.literal: Yunke sent a letter to Qiying, Yilibu, and others, saying: "The pacification settlement is already fixed, but later troubles are many; there are matters one cannot but anxiously overthink.
translations.idiomatic: Yunke wrote to Qiying, Yilibu, and the others: "Peace is settled, but many troubles remain, and some cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 英船散處粵、閩、浙、蘇較多，其中有他國糾約前來者，粵東又有新到。

translations.literal: English ships are scattered in Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu in considerable numbers; among them are some from other countries bound by treaty who have come; in eastern Guangdong there are also newly arrived ones.
translations.idiomatic: British ships are scattered widely across Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu, including vessels from other treaty powers, and fresh arrivals continue in eastern Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 倘退兵之後，或有他出效尤，或即英人託名復出，別肆要求，變幻莫測。

translations.literal: If after troops withdraw others come out imitating them, or the English themselves under borrowed names reappear with separate demands, changes are unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops withdraw, others may imitate them, or the British themselves may reappear under another name with fresh demands. Such shifts are impossible to predict.

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 洋人在粵，曾經就撫，迨給銀後，滋擾不休​​，反覆性成，前車可鑑。

translations.literal: Foreigners in Guangdong once submitted to pacification; after silver was given they harassed without cease—their fickleness is ingrained; the overturned cart ahead can be taken as mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners in Guangdong once accepted pacification, yet after payment they harassed without end. Their fickleness is well known, and the past is warning enough.

sentences.zh: 或復稱國主之言，謂馬、郭辦理不善，撤回本國，別生枝節。

translations.literal: Or again they may cite their sovereign's words, saying Ma and Guo handled matters poorly, recall them to their country, and create separate complications.
translations.idiomatic: They may again claim their sovereign's word that Ma and Guo handled affairs badly, recall them home, and raise new complications.

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 上所獲之郭逆義子陳祿，皆云雖給銀割地，決不肯不往天津，而現索馬頭不及天津，殊為可疑。

translations.literal: Chen Lu, adopted son of the rebel Guo whom the court captured, all say that though silver is given and territory cut away, they absolutely will not refuse to go to Tianjin; yet now they demand a wharf short of Tianjin—this is especially suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lu, adopted son of the captured rebel Guo, says that even after payment and cession they will still insist on going to Tianjin, yet they now demand a wharf short of Tianjin. This is highly suspicious.

sentences.zh: 能杜其北上之心，方免事後​​之悔。

translations.literal: Only if one can block their mind to go north can one avoid regret afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Only by blocking their desire to move north can we avoid later regret.

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 通商既定，自必明立章程，各省關口應輸稅課，萬一洋人仍向商船攔阻，勢不能聽其病商攘課，一經阻止，又啟釁端。

translations.literal: Once trade is fixed, regulations must clearly be established; each province's passes should pay tax dues; if by chance foreigners still intercept merchant ships, one cannot in power listen to them harming merchants and seizing dues—once stopped, strife is again opened.
translations.idiomatic: Once trade is established, regulations must be set and customs dues collected at every pass. If foreigners still intercept merchant ships, we cannot let them harm trade and seize revenue, yet stopping them may reopen conflict.

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 民人與洋人獄訟，應聽有司訊斷，萬一抗不交犯，又如粵東林如美之案，何以戢外暴而定民心？

translations.literal: Civil cases between people and foreigners should be heard and judged by the relevant offices; if by chance they resist and do not hand over offenders, as in the eastern Guangdong Lin Rumei case, how can one restrain foreign violence and settle popular hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Cases between Chinese and foreigners should be tried by local officials. If offenders are refused, as in the Lin Rumei case in Guangdong, how can foreign violence be restrained and public order secured?

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 罷兵之後，各處海口仍須設防，修造戰船砲台，添設兵伍營卡，倘洋人猜疑阻擾，以致海防不能整頓。

translations.literal: After troops are dismissed, each place's sea mouths still must set defenses, repair and build war junks and batteries, add troops and camp posts; if foreigners suspect and obstruct, causing coastal defense unable to be put in order.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops stand down, every port must still be defended, warships and batteries rebuilt, and garrisons reinforced. If foreigners suspect and obstruct us, coastal defense cannot be restored.

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 今日漢奸盡為彼用，一經通商，須治奸民。

translations.literal: Today Han traitors are all used by them; once trade is opened, traitorous people must be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese collaborators now serve the foreigners entirely. Once trade opens, traitors among our people must be controlled.

sentences.zh: 內地民人投往者，應令全數交出，聽候安插。

translations.literal: People from the interior who have gone over to them should be ordered to hand over all in full and await resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: All Chinese who have gone over to them from the interior should be required to return and await resettlement.

sentences.zh: 否則介夫洋漢之間，勢必恃洋犯法，不逞之徒，又將投入，官法難施，必尋釁隙。

translations.literal: Otherwise, standing between foreigners and Han, they will surely rely on foreigners to break the law; unruly fellows will again throw themselves in; official law will be hard to apply, and they will surely seek pretexts for quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise go-betweens between foreigners and Chinese will rely on foreign protection to break the law. Unruly men will flock to them, official justice will fail, and trouble will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 既定馬頭，除通商地面不容泊岸，倘有任意闖入，取掠牲畜婦女，民人不平，糾合抗拒，彼必歸咎於官，而興問罪之師。

translations.literal: Once the wharf is fixed, apart from the trade ground they must not anchor ashore; if some rashly break in, seize livestock and women, and the people are not at peace and gather to resist, they will surely blame the officials and raise armies to demand punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Once the wharf is fixed, foreigners must not land outside the trade zone. If they raid livestock and seize women, the people will rise in anger. The foreigners will blame the officials and send punitive forces.

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者八也。

translations.literal: This is the eighth matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 名曰通商，本非割地，而定海拆毀城垣，建造洋樓，挈眷居住，倘各省均如此，恐非通商體制，腹內之地，舉以畀人，轉瞬即非我有。

translations.literal: Called trade in name, it is fundamentally not ceding territory, yet at Dinghai city walls were torn down, foreign buildings erected, and families brought to live there; if each province were thus, I fear it is not the trade system—lands in the belly of the realm, all given to others, in an instant would no longer be ours.
translations.idiomatic: Trade in name is not cession of territory, yet at Dinghai they tore down the walls, built foreign houses, and settled their families. If every province followed suit, this would no longer be trade but the surrender of the heartland itself.

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者九也。

translations.literal: This is the ninth matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ninth worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 中國凋敝，由於漏銀出洋。

translations.literal: China's exhaustion comes from silver leaking overseas.
translations.idiomatic: China's exhaustion comes from silver draining overseas.

sentences.zh: 今各省有洋船，漏銀更甚，大利之源，勢將立竭。

translations.literal: Now each province has foreign ships; silver leaks more severely; the great source of profit will in momentum soon be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Now foreign ships reach every province, silver drains faster still, and the nation's great source of wealth will soon run dry.

sentences.zh: 會子、交子之弊政將行，國用、民用之生計已絕。

translations.literal: The bad policies of tally notes and exchange notes will soon be practiced; state use and people's livelihood will be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The evils of paper currency will follow, and both state revenue and people's livelihood will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 此不可不慮者十也。

translations.literal: This is the tenth matter that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: This is the tenth worry that cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 至於議給之款，各省分撥。

translations.literal: As for the funds agreed to be given, each province shares the allocation.
translations.idiomatic: As for the indemnity agreed upon, each province must bear its share.

sentences.zh: 浙省自軍興以來，商民捐餉賑災，寧波菁華為洋人搜括，歲事歉收，責以賂敵之款，勢必不應。

translations.literal: Zhejiang since the army arose has had merchants and people donate pay and relieve disaster; Ningbo's finest resources were searched and taken by foreigners; the year's harvest was poor—to charge them with funds to bribe the enemy will in momentum surely not be answered.
translations.idiomatic: Since the war began Zhejiang's merchants and people have donated pay and relief funds. Ningbo's wealth has been stripped by foreigners and the harvest failed. To demand indemnity payments now is impossible.

sentences.zh: 若如四川之議增糧賦，江、浙萬不能行。

translations.literal: If like Sichuan's proposal to increase grain levies, Jiangsu and Zhejiang absolutely cannot carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Raising grain taxes as proposed in Sichuan is utterly impossible in Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 故剿敵之款可捐，賂敵之款不可捐，他省完善之地可捐，浙省殘破之餘不可捐。

translations.literal: Therefore funds to suppress the enemy may be donated; funds to bribe the enemy may not be donated; intact places in other provinces may donate; Zhejiang in its broken remainder may not donate.
translations.idiomatic: Funds to fight the enemy may be raised by donation, but not funds to bribe them. Intact provinces may contribute, but ruined Zhejiang cannot.

sentences.zh: 惟亮虓之！」

translations.literal: Only make this clear!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider this clearly!"

sentences.zh: 所言並切利害。

translations.literal: What he said all cut to benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: His words all struck at the heart of the matter.

sentences.zh: 韻珂機警多智，數見浙兵不可恃，以戰事委之裕謙、奕經，專固省防，浙人德之。

translations.literal: Yunke was alert and full of wisdom; he several times saw Zhejiang troops could not be relied on, entrusted war affairs to Yijing and Campaign General Yijing, and focused on securing provincial defense; Zhejiang people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunke was shrewd and resourceful. Seeing repeatedly that Zhejiang troops could not be trusted, he left fighting to Yijing and Campaign General Yijing while focusing on provincial defense. The people of Zhejiang were grateful.

sentences.zh: 及事急，再創調停之說，而慮成議於浙，為天下詬，移禍於江蘇。

translations.literal: When affairs grew urgent he again raised mediation talk, yet feared the agreement would be made in Zhejiang, be reviled by all under Heaven, and shift disaster to Jiangsu.
