translations.idiomatic: When crisis came he again urged mediation, fearing that if peace were made in Zhejiang he would be reviled nationwide for shifting the disaster to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 然世多譏其巧於趨避。

translations.literal: Yet the age mostly ridiculed his skill at dodging and evading.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many criticized his talent for evasion.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「浙江舊未與外洋交易，與廣東情事不同。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Zhejiang formerly did not trade with the outer ocean; its situation differs from Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Zhejiang never traded with foreigners before and its situation differs from Guangdong's.

sentences.zh: 應於耆英等所議章程稍加變通，先申要約。」

translations.literal: One should slightly modify the regulations Qiying and others deliberated and first declare essential agreements."
translations.idiomatic: The regulations Qiying negotiated should be adapted somewhat, with essential terms stated first."

sentences.zh: 又籌海疆善後事宜二十四則，下議行。

translations.literal: He also planned twenty-four items of coastal postwar arrangements, which were sent down for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted twenty-four measures for postwar coastal administration, which were ordered for implementation.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，疏報廈門開市，鼓浪嶼尚有英兵棲止，恐久假不歸，請諭禁，與領事面訂預杜偷漏稽查洋眾條款。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he memorialized reporting Xiamen's market opening; Gulangyu still had English troops dwelling there—fearing long borrowing without return, he requested prohibition by edict, and face to face with the consul fixed clauses to forestall smuggling and inspect foreign crowds.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he reported the opening of Xiamen. British troops still remained on Gulangyu, and fearing they would stay indefinitely he asked for orders to remove them. With the consul he agreed on clauses to prevent smuggling and regulate foreigners.

sentences.zh: 又奏天主教流弊，請稽查傳教之地，不令藏奸；

translations.literal: He also memorialized on Catholic abuses, requesting inspection of preaching places and not allowing traitors to be hidden;
translations.idiomatic: He also reported abuses of Catholic missions and asked that preaching sites be inspected so traitors could not hide there;

sentences.zh: 或有藉端滋事，據事懲辦，不牽及習教，俾無藉口。

translations.literal: if some use pretexts to stir trouble, punish according to the facts without implicating those who merely study the religion, so there is no pretext.
translations.idiomatic: if troublemakers used religion as a pretext, they should be punished on the facts without implicating ordinary converts, leaving no excuse for complaint.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，英人始至福州，請於南台及城內烏石山建洋樓，韻珂難之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the English first reached Fuzhou and requested to build foreign halls at Nantai and within the city at Wushishan; Yunke made it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 the British first reached Fuzhou and asked to build foreign houses at Nantai and on Wushishan inside the city. Yunke resisted.

sentences.zh: 士紳見廣東爭議久不決，亦援以拒。

translations.literal: Gentry and officials, seeing Guangdong's dispute long unresolved, also cited it to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Local gentry, seeing Guangdong's entry dispute drag on unresolved, cited that precedent to refuse as well.

sentences.zh: 英人訴諸耆英，謂不踐原約，則鼓浪嶼且不退還，往復辯論，卒不能阻，而閩人歸咎於韻珂。

translations.literal: The English complained to Qiying, saying if the original agreement were not kept Gulangyu would not be returned; back and forth they argued, and in the end could not obstruct it, while Fujian people blamed Yunke.
translations.idiomatic: The British appealed to Qiying, saying that if the original treaty were not honored Gulangyu would not be returned. After repeated argument Yunke could not stop them, and the people of Fujian blamed him.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文宗即位，以病乞假，特旨罷職回籍。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the Wenzong Emperor ascended; on grounds of illness he requested leave; a special edict dismissed him from office and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30, when the Wenzong Emperor ascended the throne, Yunke asked for sick leave and was specially ordered dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，坐泉州經歷何士邠犯贓逃逸，追論寬縱，褫職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, because Quanzhou clerk He Shibin committed corruption and fled, retrospective discussion of lenient indulgence stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 he was stripped of office for leniency toward Quanzhou clerk He Shibin, who had taken bribes and fled.

sentences.zh: 同治初，召來京，以三品京堂候補。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he was summoned to the capital and made a third-rank Beijing official awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he was recalled to Beijing as a third-rank capital official awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 復乞病歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Again he requested leave for illness and returned home; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to retire on grounds of illness, went home, and died there.

sentences.zh: =牛鑑=牛鑑，字鏡堂，甘肅武威人。

translations.literal: Niu Jian, style name Jingtang, was a native of Wuwei in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jian, whose style was Jingtang, came from Wuwei in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the nineteenth year of Jiaqing, he was selected as Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in Jiaqing 19, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 道光十一年，出為雲南糧儲道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daoguang he went out as Yunnan grain storage intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 11 he was posted as Yunnan grain storage intendant.

sentences.zh: 歷山東按察使、順天府尹、陝西布政使，與巡撫不合，乞病歸。

translations.literal: He successively served as Shandong provincial judicial commissioner, Shuntian metropolitan governor, and Shaanxi provincial treasurer; he did not agree with the provincial governor and requested leave for illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial commissioner of Shandong, metropolitan governor of Shuntian, and provincial treasurer of Shaanxi. After falling out with the governor he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十八年，起授江蘇布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was recalled and appointed Jiangsu provincial treasurer, acting as provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he was recalled as provincial treasurer of Jiangsu and served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢河南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to Henan provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he was promoted to governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 整頓吏治，停分發，止攤捐；

translations.literal: He put administration in order, halted distribution assignments, and stopped surcharge levies;
translations.idiomatic: He cleaned up local administration, halted routine assignments of officials, and stopped surcharge levies;

sentences.zh: 籌銀二十萬兩，津貼瘠累十五縣；

translations.literal: raised two hundred thousand taels of silver to subsidize fifteen impoverished counties burdened with arrears;
translations.idiomatic: raised two hundred thousand taels to subsidize fifteen impoverished counties burdened with tax arrears;

sentences.zh: 築沁河堤，濬衛河：甚有政聲。

translations.literal: built the Qin River dike and dredged the Wei River: he had a strong reputation in governance.
translations.idiomatic: built dikes on the Qin River and dredged the Wei River, winning a strong reputation for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 二十一年六月，河決祥符，水圍省城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year the river broke at Xiangfu and water surrounded the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 21 the Yellow River burst at Xiangfu and flooded around the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 鑑率吏民葺城以守，規地勢洩水，賑撫災黎。

translations.literal: Jian led officials and people to repair the city for defense, planned terrain to release water, and relieved and soothed disaster victims.
translations.idiomatic: Jian led officials and people to repair the walls for defense, planned drainage according to the terrain, and relieved the flood victims.

sentences.zh: 時水分二流，一環城西南，一由東南行，均注歸德、陳州，入江南境。

translations.literal: At that time the water divided into two streams, one encircling the city's southwest, one going by the southeast, both pouring into Guide and Chenzhou and entering Jiangnan territory.
translations.idiomatic: The flood split into two streams, one circling the southwest of the city and one running southeast. Both flowed toward Guide and Chenzhou and into Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 鑑以正河斷流，決口難遽塞，議急衛省城。

translations.literal: Jian, because the main river channel was cut off and the breach could not quickly be blocked, proposed urgently defending the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Jian argued that with the main channel cut off and the breach impossible to close quickly, the urgent task was to defend the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 水漲不已，西北隅尤當衝，城垣坍陷十餘處，拋磚石成壩，絙鉅舟以御之。

translations.literal: Water rose without cease; the northwest corner especially bore the brunt; city walls collapsed in more than ten places; they cast brick and stone to form dams and roped great boats to resist it.
translations.idiomatic: The water kept rising, and the northwest corner bore the brunt. The walls collapsed in more than ten places. They threw brick and stone to form dams and moored large boats as barriers.

sentences.zh: 奇險迭出，晝夜臨陴，民感其誠，同心守護，有不受僱值者。

translations.literal: Strange perils came one after another; day and night he stood on the battlements; the people were moved by his sincerity, guarded together in one heart, and some would not accept wages.
translations.idiomatic: Perils came one after another. He stood on the walls day and night. The people were moved by his sincerity and defended together; some refused even to take wages.

sentences.zh: 當事急，河督文沖奏省城卑濕不可復居，請擇地遷移。

translations.literal: When affairs were urgent, River Conservancy Director Wen Chong memorialized that the provincial city was low and damp and could not again be inhabited, requesting to choose ground and relocate.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the crisis River Director Wen Chong reported that the capital was too low and damp to remain in and asked to relocate it elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 鑑疏言：「一月以來，困守危城，幸保無虞者，實由人心維繫。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized: "For one month, trapped defending a perilous city, the fact that we fortunately kept free of disaster truly came from popular hearts being bound together.
translations.idiomatic: Jian wrote: "For a month we have held this endangered city and kept it safe only because the people's morale has held together.

sentences.zh: 若一聞遷徙。

translations.literal: If one word of relocation is heard.
translations.idiomatic: If word of relocation spreads,

sentences.zh: 各自逃生，誰與防守？

translations.literal: each will flee for his life—who will defend with us?
translations.idiomatic: everyone will flee for his life. Who will remain to defend the city?

sentences.zh: 恐遷徙未及，水已灌城，變生俄頃，奸民乘機搶掠，法令不行，情狀不堪設想。

translations.literal: I fear before relocation is completed water will already flood the city; change will arise in an instant; treacherous people will seize the chance to plunder; law and order will not be enforced—the situation is unbearable to imagine.
translations.idiomatic: Before relocation could be completed the flood might already enter the city. Disaster would come in an instant, criminals would loot, and order would collapse beyond imagining.

sentences.zh: 節交白露，水將漸消，惟有殫竭血誠，堅忍守禦，但得料物應手，自可化險為平。」

translations.literal: The season reaches White Dew; water will gradually subside—only by exhausting heart's blood in sincerity and steadfastly enduring defense, provided materials are at hand, can danger be turned to peace."
translations.idiomatic: White Dew is near and the waters will subside. If we exhaust ourselves in honest defense and supplies are at hand, danger can still be turned to safety."

sentences.zh: 命大學士王鼎、侍郎慧成往勘。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Ding and Vice Minister Huicheng were ordered to go inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Ding and Vice Minister Huicheng were sent to inspect.

sentences.zh: 鑑與合疏言省城可守不可遷，決口可堵不可漫，並劾文沖漠視延誤狀，於是褫文沖職。

translations.literal: Jian jointly memorialized that the provincial city could be held and must not be moved, the breach could be blocked and must not be neglected, and also impeached Wen Chong for indifferent delay—thereupon Wen Chong's office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Jian jointly reported that the capital could be held and must not be abandoned, that the breach could and must be closed, and impeached Wen Chong for neglect and delay. Wen Chong was then dismissed.

sentences.zh: 秸料大集，繕治堤壩，水亦漸退，守城凡六十餘日而卒完。

translations.literal: Straw materials gathered in great numbers, dikes and dams were repaired, water also gradually receded, and defending the city for more than sixty days in the end was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Straw and timber were gathered in quantity, dikes were repaired, the waters gradually fell, and after more than sixty days of defense the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 命偕王鼎​​等興工塞決。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Wang Ding and others to start work blocking the breach.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Wang Ding and others to begin closing the breach.

sentences.zh: 會英兵犯浙江，裕謙殉於寧波，命鑑代署兩江總督，尋實授。

translations.literal: When English troops attacked Zhejiang and Yijing died a martyr's death at Ningbo, Jian was ordered to act as governor-general of the Two Jiangs, and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When British forces attacked Zhejiang and Yijing died at Ningbo, Jian was made acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs and soon received the substantive post.

sentences.zh: 十月，至蘇州受事，閱海口，偕提督陳化成治防，繕台增砲，沿海以土塘為蔽，駐四營居中策應。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached Suzhou to take office, inspected the sea mouth, together with Provincial Commander Chen Huacheng managed defenses, repaired batteries and added cannon, along the coast used earth ramparts as cover, and stationed four camps in the center to respond as needed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he took office at Suzhou, inspected the coastal defenses, and with Provincial Commander Chen Huacheng organized the fortifications, repaired batteries, added guns, built earthen ramparts along the coast, and stationed four camps to support one another.

sentences.zh: 二十二年四月，英兵既陷乍浦，遂窺吳淞口。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-second year, after English troops had taken Zhapu, they then spied on Wusong mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 22, after the British took Zhapu, they turned toward Wusong.

sentences.zh: 五月，敵艦七十餘艘來攻，鑑偕化成督戰，擊沉賊船三，西砲台及戰艦皆被毀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month more than seventy enemy ships came to attack; Jian together with Huacheng directed the battle, sank three rebel ships, and both the western battery and war junks were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month more than seventy enemy ships attacked. Jian and Huacheng directed the battle, sank three enemy vessels, but the western battery and the warships were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 敵以小舟載兵由小沙背登陸，徐州鎮總兵王志元兵先潰，化成死之。

translations.literal: The enemy used small boats to carry troops ashore at Xiaoshabei; Xuzhou Garrison Regional Commander Wang Zhiyuan's troops fled first; Huacheng died.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy landed troops in small boats at Xiaoshabei. Regional Commander Wang Zhiyuan's force broke first, and Huacheng was killed.

sentences.zh: 鑑退嘉定，而寶山、上海相繼陷。

translations.literal: Jian withdrew to Jiading, while Baoshan and Shanghai in succession fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jian withdrew to Jiading as Baoshan and Shanghai fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 又退崑山，收集潰兵。

translations.literal: He again withdrew to Kunshan and gathered fleeing troops.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew again to Kunshan and gathered the routed troops.

sentences.zh: 壽春鎮總兵尤渤守松江，敵兩次來犯，皆擊卻之。

translations.literal: Shouchun Garrison Regional Commander You Bo guarded Songjiang; the enemy twice came to attack and was both times beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander You Bo held Songjiang and twice beat back enemy attacks.

sentences.zh: 英艦聚泊吳淞口外，揚言將北犯天津。

translations.literal: English ships gathered and anchored outside Wusong mouth, proclaiming they would attack Tianjin in the north.
translations.idiomatic: British ships gathered off Wusong and announced they would strike north toward Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 六月，突入江，乘潮上駛，直越圌山關，鑑由京口退保江寧。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they suddenly entered the river, rode the tide upstream, passed straight over Tushan Pass, and Jian from Jingkou withdrew to hold Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they burst into the Yangzi, rode the tide upstream past Tushan Pass, and Jian fell back from Jingkou to defend Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 提督齊慎、劉允孝迎戰京口，不利，退守新豐。

translations.literal: Provincial Commanders Qi Shen and Liu Yunxiao met the enemy in battle at Jingkou with unfavorable result and withdrew to hold Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Commanders Qi Shen and Liu Yunxiao fought at Jingkou, were defeated, and withdrew to Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 鎮江陷，副都統海齡死之。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang fell; Vice Commander-in-Chief Hailing died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang fell and Vice Commander-in-Chief Hailing was killed.

sentences.zh: 敵艦分薄瓜洲，揚州震動，鹽運使但明倫聽商人江壽民計，賂以六十萬金，遂犯江寧，艦泊下關。

translations.literal: Enemy ships divided to press Guazhou; Yangzhou was shaken; Salt Transport Commissioner Dan Minglun listened to merchant Jiang Shoumin's plan and bribed them with six hundred thousand in gold; they then attacked Jiangning and ships anchored at Xiaguan.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy ships pressed Guazhou and Yangzhou was shaken. Salt Commissioner Dan Minglun followed merchant Jiang Shoumin's advice and paid six hundred thousand taels in bribes. The British then advanced on Jiangning and anchored at Xiaguan.

sentences.zh: 鑑初專防海口，倚陳化成，沿江鵝鼻嘴、圌山關諸要隘倉猝調兵，益無足恃。

translations.literal: Jian at first focused defense on the sea mouth and relied on Chen Huacheng; along the river at vital passes such as Ebi Mouth and Tushan Pass troops were hastily transferred, and even less could be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had focused on the coastal mouth and relied on Chen Huacheng. Vital posts along the river such as Ebi Mouth and Tushan Pass were manned only by troops rushed in at the last moment and could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 化成既死事，鑑知不能復戰，連疏請議撫。

translations.literal: After Huacheng died in service, Jian knew he could not fight again and repeatedly memorialized requesting peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: After Huacheng's death Jian knew the fight was lost and sent repeated memorials asking for peace negotiations.

sentences.zh: 耆英、伊里布先後奉命至，英人索五處通商及償款，諸臣未敢遽允；

translations.literal: Qiying and Yilibu in succession were ordered to arrive; the English demanded five places for trade and indemnity payments—the ministers did not dare quickly agree;
translations.idiomatic: Qiying and Yilibu arrived in turn on imperial orders. The British demanded five treaty ports and an indemnity, and the officials did not dare agree at once;

sentences.zh: 敵兵遂登岸，置大砲臨城，乃悉許之。

translations.literal: enemy troops then landed ashore, placed great cannon facing the city, and only then were all demands granted.
translations.idiomatic: the enemy landed, placed heavy guns facing the city, and then every demand was granted.

sentences.zh: 合疏以保全民命為請，略曰：「江寧危急，呼吸可虞，根本一摧，鄰近皖、贛、鄂、湘皆可航溯。

translations.literal: Jointly they memorialized requesting to preserve all people's lives, saying in summary: "Jiangning is perilous and can be doubted in a breath; once the root is broken, neighboring Anhui, Jiangxi, Hubei, and Hunan can all be reached by sailing upstream.
translations.idiomatic: They jointly memorialized to save the people's lives, writing: "Jiangning is in immediate peril. If this root is lost, Anhui, Jiangxi, Hubei, and Hunan can all be reached by river.

sentences.zh: 彼所請雖無厭，而通市外無他圖。

translations.literal: What they request though insatiable, apart from opening markets they have no other design.
translations.idiomatic: Their demands may be endless, but beyond opening markets they appear to have no other design.

sentences.zh: 與其結兵禍而毒生靈，曷若捐鉅帑以全大局？

translations.literal: Rather than tie military disaster and poison the living, why not donate great treasure to preserve the great situation?
translations.idiomatic: Better to pay a great indemnity and preserve the whole situation than to prolong war and ruin the people.

sentences.zh: 廈門敵軍雖退，尚未收復。

translations.literal: At Xiamen enemy troops though withdrawn have not yet been recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy has withdrawn from Xiamen, but the place is not yet recovered.

sentences.zh: 香港、鼓浪嶼、定海、招寶山仍未退還，使任其久踞逡巡，不如歸我土地。

translations.literal: Hong Kong, Gulangyu, Dinghai, and Zhaobaoshan are still not returned; to let them long occupy and linger is inferior to returning our territory.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Kong, Gulangyu, Dinghai, and Zhaobaoshan are still not returned. Better to have our land back than let them linger in occupation.

sentences.zh: 既原循例輸稅，即為悔禍鄉風。

translations.literal: Since they are willing to pay tax according to precedent, that is repentance of disaster and village custom.
translations.idiomatic: If they are willing to pay customs duties as before, that itself shows repentance and a return to proper relations.

sentences.zh: 此後彼因自護租岸，我即以捍蔽海疆，未始非國家之福。

translations.literal: Hereafter because they protect their leased shore for themselves, we may use it to shield the maritime frontier—not necessarily not the state's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, as they protect their leased ports for their own trade, we may use that to shield the coast. That need not be a loss to the state.

sentences.zh: 所請平禮虛文，不妨假借。

translations.literal: The requested equal ceremonial empty forms may without harm be borrowed.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial concessions they request may be granted in form if necessary.

sentences.zh: 事定之後，亦應釋俘囚以堅和好，寬脅從以安反側。」

translations.literal: After affairs are settled, captives should also be released to solidify good relations, and the coerced leniently treated to settle those who turned."
translations.idiomatic: After peace is settled, prisoners should be released to strengthen goodwill, and those coerced into service treated leniently to calm unrest."

sentences.zh: 並附詳條目以聞。

translations.literal: Detailed articles were also attached for report.
translations.idiomatic: Detailed articles were attached to the memorial.

sentences.zh: 八月，和議成，英兵悉退出海洋。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the peace agreement was made and English troops all withdrew to the ocean.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month peace was concluded and all British forces withdrew to sea.

sentences.zh: 尋以貽誤封疆罪，褫職逮問，讞大辟，二十四年，釋之，命赴河南中牟河工效力。

translations.literal: Soon on the charge of bringing disaster on the frontier his office was stripped and he was arrested for inquiry; judgment was death; in the twenty-fourth year he was released and ordered to go to Henan Zhongmou river works to render service.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon stripped of office and arrested for having failed the frontier. Sentence was death, but in year 24 he was released and ordered to serve on the Zhongmou river works in Henan.

sentences.zh: 工竣，予七品頂戴，以六部主事用，回籍。

translations.literal: When the work was completed he was given seventh-rank cap button and used as a director in one of the Six Ministries, then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he was given seventh-rank insignia and appointed a director in one of the Six Ministries, then returned home.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪北擾，予五品頂戴，署河南按察使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, when Guangdong bandits disturbed the north, he was given fifth-rank cap button and acted as Henan provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3, when Guangdong rebels raided northward, he was given fifth-rank insignia and served as acting judicial commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 四年，命卸任，勸捐募勇，赴陳州，偕徐廣縉剿捻匪，破潁州賊李士林於阜陽方家集，焚其巢，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to leave office, urged donations and recruited braves, went to Chenzhou, together with Xu Guangjin suppressed Nian bandits, defeated Yingzhou rebel Li Shilin at Fangjiaji in Fuyang, burned his lair, and was given judicial commissioner rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he left office, raised donations and recruits, went to Chenzhou, and with Xu Guangjin fought the Nian rebels. He defeated Li Shilin at Fangjiaji in Fuyang, burned his base, and was given judicial commissioner rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，又破之於霍丘三河，士林尋於湖北就撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again defeated him at Sanhe in Huoqiu; Shilin soon submitted to pacification in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he defeated him again at Sanhe in Huoqiu. Shilin soon submitted in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 鑑深得河南民心，前勸捐中牟大工，得錢二百萬緡，至是集軍餉复及百萬。

translations.literal: Jian deeply won Henan popular hearts; earlier in urging donations for the Zhongmou great works he obtained two million strings of cash; by now in gathering army pay he again reached one million.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had won the hearts of the people of Henan. His earlier fund drive for the Zhongmou works had raised two million strings of cash, and he now raised another million for army funds.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加二品頂戴。

translations.literal: Merit was narrated and he was given second-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was given second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 以病乞歸。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 8.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：顏伯燾懷抱忠憤，而無克敵致果之具。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Yan Bozao harbored loyal indignation but lacked the means to overcome the enemy and achieve results.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Yan Bozao was full of loyal indignation but lacked the means to defeat the enemy and win victory.

sentences.zh: 怡良不附和琦善，亦無建樹。

translations.literal: Yi Liang did not echo Qishan, yet also had no achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Liang did not side with Qishan, yet he too achieved nothing of note.

sentences.zh: 祁𡎴依違和戰之間，苟全而已。

translations.literal: Qi Jun wavered between peace and war and sought only to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jun wavered between war and peace and sought only to save himself.

sentences.zh: 劉韻珂以術馭人，陰主和議。

translations.literal: Liu Yunke used craft to control others and secretly upheld peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yunke manipulated others by craft and secretly favored peace.

sentences.zh: 牛鑑以循吏處危疆，身敗名裂。

translations.literal: Niu Jian as a model official faced a perilous frontier and body failed and name was torn.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jian, a conscientious local official placed on a desperate frontier, ended in ruin and disgrace.

sentences.zh: 要之籌邊大計，朝廷​​無成算，則膺封圻之寄者為益難，況人事之未盡乎？

translations.literal: In sum, in planning the great frontier policy, if the court has no settled plan, then those who bear the commission of border posts find it still harder—how much more when human affairs are not exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: In short, when the court had no settled frontier policy, those entrusted with border posts faced an even harder task—and how much harder when human effort fell short?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 論世者當觀其微也。

translations.literal: Those who judge the age should observe its subtle signs.
translations.idiomatic: Those who judge an age must read its subtle signs.
